question.text: The polar coordinate of a point $P$ is $\left(2,-\frac{\pi} {4}\right)$ The polar coordinate of the point $Q$ which is such that line joining $P Q$ is bisected perpendicularly by the initial line, is

solution.text: Since, $Q$ is the point for which $P Q$ is bisected perpendicularly by the initial line $(X$ -axis). Therefore, $Q$ will be the image of $P$ in $X$ -axis $\therefore$ Coordinates of $Q$ is $(2, \pi / 4)$
